about: Country figures for the AI World Map (pages/ai-world-map.html). Every value comes from the source named on its layer; sec 1 = read from a secondary reproduction of the primary report (shown with ⚠️). Countries not listed have no figure in that source, which is not the same as zero.

layers.title: Private AI investment, 2025

For 2026 so far, see the AI Investment Tracker (venture totals Q1–Q3).

layers.title: Share of the world's AI compute received, 2022 → June 2026 (H100-equivalents)
layers.source: Epoch AI, AI Chip Imports explorer (launched 27 Oct 2026) and its methodology page
layers.note: Modelled estimates, not an inventory. Of 27.4M H100-equivalents that arrived 2022 → Jun 2026, 19.8M went to the US; its yearly share rose from ~60% (2022–24) to 72% (2025) and 78% (H1 2026). China (incl. domestic chips) holds 18.2% of chip units but 9.6% of compute. The EU as a bloc is 5%; Malaysia ~2% (Epoch thread); no other country above 2%.

layers.title: Sovereign AI compute: GPUs in government-owned or government-funded national systems (Nov 2026)

detail.840: US Department of Energy flagship systems only: Aurora 63,744 Intel GPUs (Argonne), El Capitan 44,544 AMD MI300A (Livermore), Frontier 37,632 AMD MI250X (Oak Ridge)
detail.356: IndiaAI Mission common compute: 38,231 GPUs onboarded (government reply in Parliament, Mar 2026); a PIB factsheet reports 45,000+ by Jun 2026 ⚠️. Subsidised access to GPUs owned by private providers
detail.276: JUPITER (Jülich, EuroHPC): 23,536 NVIDIA GH200 in its June 2025 TOP500 run (~24,000 announced)
detail.410: About 10,500 NVIDIA GPUs bought by the government in 2025 for public use ⚠️ secondary
detail.826: Isambard-AI (Bristol, AI Research Resource): 5,448 NVIDIA GH200
detail.250: Jean Zay H100 extension (GENCI/CNRS): 1,456 NVIDIA H100; older V100/A100 partitions not counted
detail.246: LUMI (CSC, EuroHPC): 11,912 AMD MI250X ⚠️ count via an aggregator (Flopper.io)
detail.756: Alps (CSCS): 10,752 NVIDIA GH200 ⚠️ from the operator's node count, not re-read in this session
detail.724: MareNostrum 5 accelerated partition (BSC, EuroHPC): 4,480 NVIDIA H100 ⚠️ count via an aggregator (Flopper.io)
detail.158: Nano 4 (NCHC, national lab; launched 1 Jun 2026): 1,700+ NVIDIA H200 (pre-launch figure ⚠️) + 2 GB200 NVL72 racks (144 Blackwell GPUs); an HGX B300 system not counted
detail.643: Sber (majority state-owned) Christofari Neo: 700+ NVIDIA A100 bought before sanctions ⚠️ secondary. Not counted: Yandex's three supercomputers (3,776 A100, a private company; its data centres were hit by drone strikes in Oct 2026). No government total published; export controls block new Western GPUs
detail.076: Santos Dumont (LNCC, 2025 upgrade funded by Petrobras): 62 blades × 4 NVIDIA H100 = 248 H100 in its largest partition (our arithmetic from the published blade count); the AMD MI300A partition is not counted

layers.source: Official system pages and announcements per country (see each country's line); India from the Indian government; South Korea from secondary reporting ⚠️
layers.note: Solid bubbles = operating; dashed rings = announced or under way (not added to the totals). Counts accelerators in named national systems, not all compute a country can reach, and mixes GPU generations (an H100 ≠ an MI250X). China publishes compute only in EFLOPS, not GPUs, so it is listed under "Disclosed in other units" with no bubble. Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN and the UAE's G42 are state-owned or state-backed companies; no operating GPU count for either has been published, so they appear only as plans. Canada's C$890M sovereign compute programme and the EU AI Gigafactories have no chip counts yet. GPU counts for Frontier, Aurora, ABCI 3.0 and Alps come from their operators' published node counts and could not be re-read from this sandbox.

784: Stargate UAE (G42/Khazna with OpenAI, Oracle, NVIDIA): ~100,000 GB300 announced for the 1 GW cluster; first 200 MW expected online Q4 2026, not yet documented as operating (Oct 2026) ⚠️
682: HUMAIN (PIF-owned): up to ~27,000 NVIDIA GPUs over 84 MW through 2027 (first phase ~6,000 B300 from Q4 2026, announced Oct 2026). AMD MI355X systems went live 31 Aug 2026, count not disclosed
356: IndiaAI: about 20,000 additional GPUs under process (13 Mar 2026), on top of the 38,231 onboarded
410: Haenam national AI computing centre: 15,000+ advanced GPUs planned by 2028 ⚠️
380: IT4LIA AI factory: 8,000+ NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, contracted Apr 2026 ⚠️
076: PBIA national AI supercomputer at Macaíba (LNCC, ~R$1.06B): about 5,000 GPUs per an earlier ministry estimate ⚠️; reports differ on 2026 vs 2027 and on the budget

other.156: No GPU count published. China reports national intelligent computing capacity of 2,185 EFLOPS (FP16) at end-June 2026 (MIIT), built through the state-led 'East Data, West Computing' programme: 8 national hubs, 10 clusters, 17 approved regional nodes; target 9,800 EFLOPS by 2030. That total includes commercial capacity, so it is not a sovereign-only GPU figure. Epoch AI estimates China received 9.6% of the world's AI compute 2022 → Jun 2026 (see the ⚡ AI compute tab).

layers.title: Model releases tracked on this site, by lab headquarters
layers.source: This site's Model Release Map (each release links its own source); lab → headquarters country is our assignment
layers.note: Counts every release in our dataset (LLM, image, video, speech, world models), Jun 2017 → Nov 2026. Google DeepMind is counted under the United States (parent company), although DeepMind is headquartered in London. BigScience (an international collaboration) is not counted.
